visual_verification.note: Vision review complements deterministic assertions and does not prove assistive-technology usability or real-user success.

five_whys: Why could the first test pass if a visual variant argument was ignored? Assertions covered only shared content and did not inspect variant-specific confirmation copy.
Why was shared content the only assertion? The first scenario was designed around the invariant interaction path and treated treatment coverage as inherited from existing tests.
Why was that insufficient? The scenario evidence claimed all three treatments without tying each result to a variant-specific observable.
Why could the test be flaky after capture? It tapped Actions after confirmation appeared without explicitly waiting for the capture sheet to dismiss.
Root cause: the initial scenario contract separated behavioral invariants from treatment and transition-state checks, and the test did not encode the UI state boundary.
corrections: Assert the expected confirmation copy for each variant and retain confirmation screenshots.
Wait for the Actions button after confirmation before opening the review flow.
Generate trace attachments with JSONSerialization and derive result booleans from observed UI state.
Record the tested source commit separately from the later evidence commit.
recurrence_guards: ScenarioValidationTests now fails if a treatment-specific confirmation is not rendered.
Scenario documentation and test code require an explicit state wait before the next interaction.
Evidence records full tested source provenance and variant-specific screenshots.

verification_incident.summary: The first matrix attempt ran iPhone and iPad xcodebuild commands in parallel, causing shared DerivedData build-database contention; the iPhone command also hit the initial 120-second shell timeout.
five_whys: Why did the initial matrix fail? The iPad build saw a locked build database and the iPhone command was interrupted by timeout.
Why was the database locked? Two xcodebuild processes shared the same DerivedData database.
Why did they share it? The destination matrix was launched in parallel without isolated DerivedData paths.
Why was parallel execution used? The local orchestration did not encode Xcode's shared-build-database constraint.
Root cause: the validation workflow lacked serialized destination execution and a timeout sized for UI tests.
verification_incident.immediate_correction: Reran destinations sequentially with a 300-second timeout.
verification_incident.recurrence_guard: The scenario-validation documentation requires sequential xcodebuild execution when using the default DerivedData location; final reruns passed.
